title: Research 6/9: administrative and mercantile precedent - chanceries, guilds, lex mercatoria, Venice's councils
description: Research agenda item 6 (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:54). How did non-judicial bodies maintain decisional consistency without formal courts? Research at minimum: chancery and registry practice (the register as the memory of the institution), guild ordinances and their internal dispute settlement, the lex mercatoria and merchant courts at the fairs (including the Rolls of Oleron and Hanseatic practice), Venice's own councils (the Senate, the Council of Ten, the Quarantie, the ducal promissione as a written constraint on the office rather than the officeholder), and modern administrative-agency precedent and published-guidance practice. The brief judges these likely closer to our topology than modern judiciaries. Output docs/precedent-research/06-administrative-mercantile-precedent.md. Web research, tagged claims, mandatory implications section.

Do NOT create or edit docs/precedent-research/README.md - that index is owned solely by the epic join T-348 (F1 single-owner rule).

WEB RESEARCH IS REQUIRED (coordinator decision D7): at least 5 named sources, of which at least 3 are primary (a judgment with its case name and citation, a statute or code article, an official practice statement or court rule, or a named-author treatise / peer-reviewed article). Every source is listed in a final Sources section with a retrievable identifier (case name plus citation, or URL plus retrieval date). Parametric-only claims with no locatable source are tagged SPECULATION, never ESTABLISHED.

EVERY substantive claim carries exactly one tag: ESTABLISHED (attributable to a named source in the Sources section), ANALOGY (a mapping from legal doctrine onto agent mechanics - the mapping is this agent's inference, not the source's claim), or SPECULATION (neither). An untagged substantive claim is a defect and grounds for REJECT. Basis: roadmap Part V principle 5, no fabricated rigor (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:96).

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Implications for the agent harness': map each finding onto the real substrate by name - blackboard task IDs (T-xxx), the three roles (thinker, worker, verifier) plus coordinator, and the four authority tiers of coordinator decision D4 (1 operator, 2 constitutional, 3 verdicted, 4 single-agent). For each finding state which schema field, CLI subcommand, or protocol rule it demands, or state explicitly that it demands none.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Extends, does not duplicate': for every doctrine that already has a partial implementation in this repo, cite it by file:line and say whether the finding EXTENDS the existing record or would DUPLICATE it. The candidates the scout already located: note taxonomy DECISION/DEVIATION/TRADEOFF/OPEN-QUESTION (ORCHESTRATION.md:69-77), the reopen verb with its mandatory-reasoning gate (.harness/bin/blackboard.py:470-517, ORCHESTRATION.md:58-67), the P-number ledger (state.json evolution.accepted_mutations), prose P-number citations in ORCHESTRATION.md, recontext.py append-only cited-evidence log, events.jsonl semantic event floor. MUST make the Goody archive thesis concrete rather than decorative (roadmap Part VII: writing constitutes the state, not merely records it): name what changes in this harness the moment a decision is written to a registry with a stable ID instead of living in a task note - and name what does NOT change.

MUST address the strongest structural analogy the brief itself invites: the ducal promissione as a constraint on the office independent of the officeholder maps onto claude.md/gemini.md and PRECEDENT.md constraining any agent regardless of engine or model - state explicitly whether that mapping is ESTABLISHED, ANALOGY, or SPECULATION.
MUST include at least one case where a non-judicial precedent system FAILED to hold consistency and say why - this feeds T-336 and T-344.
